The paper derives accurate formulas for the reflected wave phase as a function of small displacements of the boundaries between the coating layers.
The authors calculate the spectral density of coating Brownian noise using the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem.
The number of Ta2O5 layers in the coating is assumed to be N = 20, and the number of SiO2 layers is N = 19 plus a cap layer.
The refractive indices used are n_1 = 2.035 for Ta2O5 and n_2 = 1.45 for SiO2.

For the Advanced LIGO mirror geometry (radius R = 0.17 m, height H = 0.20 m, beam radius w = 0.06 m), the accurate calculation gives a 17% smaller Brownian noise spectral density compared to the approximate approach.
The authors also consider a Khalili etalon design with a smaller number of front surface layers, which is expected to further reduce the Brownian noise contribution.
The paper suggests that the explicit formulas can be used to optimize the coating layer thicknesses for thermal noise reduction, including both Brownian and thermorefractive noise.
The authors note that non-quarter wavelength coatings, as proposed by I. Pinto, can also be analyzed using the presented approach to reduce thermal coating noise.
